bug_semantics: Authenticated Krayin CRM users can read, modify, and delete other users' person/contact records by substituting an arbitrary person id on PersonController object endpoints. show(), edit(), update(), and destroy() load or mutate via PersonRepository::findOrFail($id)/update($id)/delete($id) and never compare persons.user_id to bouncer()->getAuthorizedUserIds(). List and search already scope by owner (PersonDataGrid and search()), so Individual/Group view-permission users who cannot see a contact in the grid can still hit GET /admin/contacts/persons/view/{id}, GET/PUT /admin/contacts/persons/edit/{id}, and DELETE /admin/contacts/persons/{id}. This is CWE-639 BOLA/IDOR. CVE.org state is PUBLISHED; GHSA withdrawn_at is null; NVD status is Analyzed.
flaw_origin: The unguarded id-keyed person access was first written on 2021-04-19 in 5666961a54370c577de7ad3e718716626dedb980 (jitendra <jitendra@webkul.com>, 'All attribute type added, person and organizaton creation completed'). That commit turned PersonController from index-only into CRUD and added edit($id) { findOrFail($id); return edit view } and update(..., $id) { personRepository->update(request()->all(), $id) } with no ownership check. destroy() later copied the same pattern (f450fe7d, 2021-05-12) and show() did likewise (5cf3ebc6, 2024-08-06). Sales-owner user_id plus list/search bouncer scoping landed in 57b53f31 (2024-08-14) without adding object-level checks, converting the original missing-authz lookup into cross-owner BOLA. Those later commits are extensions/refactors, not the first write of the vulnerable lines.

CVE.org is PUBLISHED and NVD is Analyzed, so this is not a withdrawn/false advisory. Later destroy() and show() copies, the 2024 sales-owner/user_id addition, and signature refactors are not BICs. The 2021 commit is a large feature commit but a single-parent first-write with no decomposable public members, so it is a valid BIC.
